- The subcommittee has completed its review of the Marketplace Seller Dispute Resolution Policy. A summary of the review and the recommended updated policy were circulated to all Board members on 8 March 2023. Discussion and adoption under Item 6 of this agenda.

5. MARKET MANAGER’S REPORT

The Market Manager (position currently vacant; duties covered by M. Chen and R. Patel on an interim basis) submitted a written report, circulated with the agenda.

- March market held on Sunday 5 March: 148 stallholders (capacity 150). Estimated attendance: 4,200.
- Two incidents were reported to the market office on the day:
  - Incident 03-05-001: A stallholder selling handmade soaps was found to be using fragrance oils that were not listed on their product safety data sheets. The stallholder was asked to remove the affected products and provided the correct documentation by the end of the day.
  - Incident 03-05-002: A customer complained that a food stall had charged a different price at the till than displayed on the menu board. The stallholder refunded the difference and adjusted the menu board immediately.
- Both incidents were resolved on the day without escalation to the Dispute Resolution Subcommittee. However, the Manager noted that the current policy does not clearly set out timeframes for responding to written complaints, and this has been identified as a gap in the review.
R. Patel noted that the interim Market Manager’s report had flagged the lack of clear timeframes as a gap, and that the proposed policy appeared to address this. He asked whether there had been any consultation with stallholders. A. Kowalski advised that the subcommittee had circulated a draft to the stallholder representative group in early February, and had received seven responses. Four were supportive, two suggested a longer deadline of ten business days, and one suggested that the deadline should not start until the complainant had provided all requested documentation. The subcommittee had considered these responses and had decided to retain the five business day deadline, but had added a note to the policy clarifying that the deadline would only commence once the complaint had been acknowledged by the market office and all relevant documentation had been received.

M. Chen asked whether the five business day deadline was consistent with the practice of other markets in the area. A. Kowalski said that the subcommittee had spoken informally with the coordinators of two neighbouring community markets, and that one used a seven day deadline while the other had no formal deadline at all. She noted that the subcommittee believed the five business day deadline struck a reasonable balance between allowing parties time to prepare their case and ensuring disputes were resolved promptly.

There being no further discussion, the Chair moved to the adoption of the revised policy.

Moved: A. Kowalski
Seconded: S. Hartley

Motion: That the Board adopt the Marketplace Seller Dispute Resolution Policy v4, as circulated with the agenda, and that it take effect from 1 April 2023.

The Board agreed that the Market Manager’s interim team would look into recruiting a volunteer to manage social media, and that in the meantime the market office would post basic updates.

She noted that the application had been received after the closing date but that the subcommittee had agreed to consider it given the short timeframe of the funding round. The Board noted this.
10.2 J. Okafor advised that the average refund value across all three years was approximately $198. She noted that a threshold of $250 would capture roughly 70 per cent of refunds currently issued, while a higher threshold of $300 would capture approximately 82 per cent. She cautioned that the sample size was small and that the figures did not include refunds processed outside the formal disputes process.

10.3 P. Nguyen asked whether the threshold would apply per dispute or per transaction. T. Withers confirmed that the policy as drafted applied per dispute, meaning that a single dispute involving multiple transactions would be assessed against the total value of the dispute. She noted that this had been clarified in the policy wording following feedback from the Stallholder Advisory Group.

10.4 R. Delacruz expressed concern that a threshold of $250 might be too high for low-value items, such as small produce stalls, where a single dispute could exceed the threshold only rarely. He suggested that the Board consider a two-tier approach, with a lower threshold for perishable goods and a higher threshold for durable goods. J. Okafor noted that this would add complexity to the disputes process and that the current draft did not distinguish between goods types.

10.5 S. Hartley noted that the Grants Subcommittee had dealt with a similar issue in its own funding criteria, where a single threshold had been retained for simplicity despite differing project sizes. She said that the subcommittee had found that applicants adapted to a clear, published threshold more readily than to a sliding scale.

10.6 M. Fotu asked whether the threshold would apply to refunds issued by mutual agreement between the buyer and the seller, or only to refunds determined by the disputes panel. T. Withers advised that the threshold applied to refunds determined by the panel. Refunds agreed directly between buyer and seller would remain outside the policy, provided the seller notified the market office within five business days of the agreement.

10.7 The Chair invited T. Withers to comment on the operational impact of the proposed threshold. T. Withers advised that the market office currently processed an average of two to three disputes per week during peak trading periods. She noted that the current informal process required the Market Manager to review each dispute individually, and that a clear threshold would allow the office to fast-track disputes below the threshold without a full panel review. She estimated that this would reduce the average time to resolution from nine business days to approximately five business days for disputes below the threshold.

She explained that the increase was based on the higher average refund value observed in the current financial year, and that the contingency would be reviewed at the half-year mark.

This charter establishes the structure, powers, and operating rules of the Marrickville Community Market Board (MCMB) and its subcommittees. The charter is binding on all members, office holders, and staff of the Board. Amendments appear in the margin beside the section they affect.

---

PART 1 – NAME, PURPOSE, AND POWERS

1.1 The body corporate shall be known as the Marrickville Community Market Board (MCMB), hereafter "the Board."

1.2 The Board operates the Marrickville Community Market precinct, comprising the Saturday growers' market, the Sunday craft and second-hand market, the community kitchen, and the storage and loading areas bounded by Illawarra Road and the railway corridor.

1.3 The purposes of the Board are:
(a) to provide a safe, accessible, and welcoming market environment for stallholders, shoppers, and the wider Marrickville community;
(b) to manage the market precinct in a financially responsible and environmentally sustainable manner;
(c) to support local producers, makers, and small businesses;
(d) to resolve disputes and address safety concerns in a fair, timely, and transparent manner; and
(e) to maintain the market as a community asset in accordance with the values of the Inner West Council.

---

PART 2 – MEMBERSHIP

2.1 The Board shall consist of no fewer than five (5) and no more than nine (9) voting members.

2.2 Membership categories:
(a) Elected members – up to five (5), elected at the Annual General Meeting;
(b) Council-appointed members – up to two (2), appointed by the Inner West Council;
(c) Community representatives – up to two (2), co-opted by the Board for their skills or community links.

2.3 The following persons are ineligible for membership:
(a) persons who are undischarged bankrupts;
(b) persons who have been convicted of an offence involving dishonesty within the preceding five (5) years;
(c) persons who are employees of the Board, other than the Market Manager who may attend meetings in an advisory capacity; and
(d) persons who hold a stallholder licence with the Market and are in arrears of fees or under active suspension.

2.5 A member may resign by written notice to the Secretary. The Board may remove a member by resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of the remaining members, on grounds of:
(a) three (3) consecutive unexcused absences from Board meetings;
(b) serious breach of this charter or the Code of Conduct; or
(c) conduct that brings the Board into disrepute.

2.6 The Board shall maintain a current Membership Register, to be reviewed at the first meeting of each financial year.

---

PART 3 – OFFICE HOLDERS

The charter specifies that the Trust and Safety Committee has a meeting_quorum of 3 members. Record status: current.

3.1 At the first meeting following each AGM, the Board shall elect from among its members:
(a) a Chair;
(b) a Deputy Chair;
(c) a Secretary; and
(d) a Treasurer.

3.2 The Chair presides at all meetings of the Board. In the Chair's absence, the Deputy Chair presides. If both are absent, the members present shall elect a chair for that meeting from among themselves.

3.3 The Secretary is responsible for:
(a) issuing notices of meetings;
(b) keeping minutes and the attendance register;
(c) maintaining the Membership Register and the Subcommittee Register; and
(d) lodging required documents with the NSW Registrar of Community Organisations.

3.5 Office holders serve for one (1) year and may be re-elected.

---

---

PART 5 – SUBCOMMITTEES

5.1 The Board may establish subcommittees to carry out specific functions. Subcommittees report to the Board and act within the terms of reference set by the Board.

5.2 Subcommittees shall be established by resolution of the Board, which shall specify:
(a) the subcommittee's name and purpose;
(b) the number of members and how they are appointed;
(c) the quorum for meetings of the subcommittee;
(d) the powers delegated to the subcommittee; and
(e) the reporting arrangements and review date.
PART 5 – SUBCOMMITTEES (continued)

5.3 Each subcommittee shall appoint one of its members as Convenor, who is responsible for:
(a) calling meetings of the subcommittee;
(b) preparing an agenda in consultation with the Board liaison member, where one has been appointed;
(c) ensuring minutes are kept and lodged with the Secretary within seven (7) days of each meeting; and
(d) presenting the subcommittee’s report to the Board at the next ordinary Board meeting.

5.4 A subcommittee may co-opt additional persons with relevant expertise, provided that:
(a) co-opted members do not count toward the subcommittee’s quorum;
(b) co-opted members have no voting rights; and
(c) the number of co-opted members does not exceed the number of appointed members.

5.5 Unless otherwise specified in the terms of reference, subcommittees shall meet at least once every two (2) months. Additional meetings may be called by the Convenor or at the request of the Board.

5.6 The Board may dissolve or reconstitute a subcommittee at any time by resolution. Upon dissolution, the subcommittee shall deliver all records and any unspent funds to the Secretary within fourteen (14) days.

5.7 Standing subcommittees as at the date of adoption of this charter:

(a) Finance and Audit Subcommittee – oversees the Market’s budget, financial reporting, and the annual independent review; quorum of three (3) members;
(b) Trust and Safety Subcommittee – oversees stallholder compliance, incident review, and the development of safety procedures; quorum of three (3) members;
(c) Events and Promotion Subcommittee – advises on market programming, marketing, and community engagement; quorum of three (3) members; and
(d) Membership and Conduct Subcommittee – reviews applications for stallholder licences, handles complaints, and makes recommendations on disciplinary matters; quorum of three (3) members.

5.8 Each standing subcommittee shall review its terms of reference at least once every two (2) years and report any proposed changes to the Board for approval.

---

PART 6 – MEETINGS OF THE BOARD

6.1 Ordinary meetings of the Board shall be held at least once every two (2) months, at a time and place determined by the Board. The schedule of meetings for each financial year shall be adopted at the first Board meeting of that year.

6.2 The Secretary shall give at least seven (7) days’ written notice of each ordinary meeting, including the agenda. Notice may be given by electronic means to the address last notified by each member.

6.3 Special meetings may be called by the Chair, or by any three (3) members of the Board, by written request to the Secretary. The Secretary shall give at least forty-eight (48) hours’ notice of a special meeting, together with the business to be considered. No other business may be transacted at a special meeting.

6.4 A meeting of the Board is quorate if at least half of the current members, or five (5) members, whichever is the lesser, are present. For the avoidance of doubt, the quorum for the Trust and Safety Subcommittee remains as set out in its terms of reference.

6.5 Questions arising at a meeting shall be decided by a majority of votes of members present and voting. Each member has one (1) vote. In the case of an equality of votes, the Chair has a second or casting vote.

6.6 A member who has a material personal interest in a matter before the Board shall:
(a) disclose the nature of the interest before the matter is discussed;
(b) not be present while the matter is being considered, unless invited by the remaining members to assist; and
(c) not vote on the matter.

6.7 The Board may pass a resolution without a meeting if the resolution is signed or otherwise agreed in writing by all members entitled to vote on it. Such a resolution is taken to have been passed at a meeting of the Board held on the day the last member signs or agrees.

6.8 Minutes shall be kept of each meeting, including the names of members present, the matters considered, and the decisions made. Draft minutes shall be circulated within fourteen (14) days of the meeting and confirmed at the next ordinary meeting.

R. Patel noted that the interim Market Manager’s report had flagged the lack of clear timeframes as a gap, and that the proposed policy appeared to address this. He asked whether there had been any consultation with stallholders. A. Kowalski advised that the subcommittee had circulated a draft to the stallholder representative group in early February, and had received seven responses. Four were supportive, two suggested a longer deadline of ten business days, and one suggested that the deadline should not start until the complainant had provided all requested documentation. Kowalski said that the subcommittee had spoken informally with the coordinators of two neighbouring community markets, and that one used a seven day deadline while the other had no formal deadline at all. She noted that the subcommittee believed the five business day deadline struck a reasonable balance between allowing parties time to prepare their case and ensuring disputes were resolved promptly.

There being no further discussion, the Chair moved to the adoption of the revised policy.

10.2 J. Okafor advised that the average refund value across all three years was approximately $198. She noted that a threshold of $250 would capture roughly 70 per cent of refunds currently issued, while a higher threshold of $300 would capture approximately 82 per cent. She cautioned that the sample size was small and that the figures did not include refunds processed outside the formal disputes process.

10.3 P. Nguyen asked whether the threshold would apply per dispute or per transaction. T. Withers confirmed that the policy as drafted applied per dispute, meaning that a single dispute involving multiple transactions would be assessed against the total value of the dispute. She noted that this had been clarified in the policy wording following feedback from the Stallholder Advisory Group.

10.4 R. Delacruz expressed concern that a threshold of $250 might be too high for low-value items, such as small produce stalls, where a single dispute could exceed the threshold only rarely. He suggested that the Board consider a two-tier approach, with a lower threshold for perishable goods and a higher threshold for durable goods. J. Okafor noted that this would add complexity to the disputes process and that the current draft did not distinguish between goods types.

10.5 S. Hartley noted that the Grants Subcommittee had dealt with a similar issue in its own funding criteria, where a single threshold had been retained for simplicity despite differing project sizes. She said that the subcommittee had found that applicants adapted to a clear, published threshold more readily than to a sliding scale.

10.6 M. Fotu asked whether the threshold would apply to refunds issued by mutual agreement between the buyer and the seller, or only to refunds determined by the disputes panel. T. Withers advised that the threshold applied to refunds determined by the panel. Refunds agreed directly between buyer and seller would remain outside the policy, provided the seller notified the market office within five business days of the agreement.

10.7 The Chair invited T. Withers to comment on the operational impact of the proposed threshold. T. Withers advised that the market office currently processed an average of two to three disputes per week during peak trading periods. She noted that the current informal process required the Market Manager to review each dispute individually, and that a clear threshold would allow the office to fast-track disputes below the threshold without a full panel review. She estimated that this would reduce the average time to resolution from nine business days to approximately five business days for disputes below the threshold.

10.8 J. Okafor tabled a revised budget line for the 2023–24 financial year, reflecting an increase in the disputes contingency from $6,000 to $7,500. She explained that the increase was based on the higher average refund value observed in the current financial year, and that the contingency would be reviewed at the half-year mark.

According to the March 2023 minutes, the Marketplace Seller Dispute Resolution Policy v4 sets the refund_threshold_aud at 250 AUD. Record status: current.

10.9 P. Nguyen moved that the Board adopt a refund threshold of $250 under the Marketplace Seller Dispute Resolution Policy v4, with the threshold to be reviewed annually as part of the policy review cycle. The motion was seconded by S. Hartley.

**Amendment:** R. Delacruz moved an amendment to reduce the threshold to $200, citing concerns about the impact on small stallholders. The amendment was seconded by M. Fotu.

**Vote on the amendment:**
- In favour: R. Delacruz, M. Fotu (2)
- Against: A. Whitlam, J. Okafor, P. Nguyen, S. Hartley, K. Brennan (5)

**Vote on the substantive motion:**
- In favour: A. Whitlam, J. Okafor, P. Nguyen, S. Hartley, K. Brennan (5)
- Against: R. Delacruz, M. Fotu (2)

The motion was carried.

10.10 The Board noted that the Marketplace Seller Dispute Resolution Policy v4 sets the refund threshold at 250 AUD. The Secretary was directed to update the policy register to record the threshold as current, effective from 1 April 2023. The policy will be circulated to all registered stallholders and posted on the market website.

documents.content:
Adopted 14 March 2016
Amended 22 August 2018
Amended 9 June 2021
Amended 3 November 2023

This charter establishes the structure, powers, and operating rules of the Marrickville Community Market Board (MCMB) and its subcommittees. The charter is binding on all members, office holders, and staff of the Board. Amendments appear in the margin beside the section they affect.

---

PART 1 – NAME, PURPOSE, AND POWERS

1.1 The body corporate shall be known as the Marrickville Community Market Board (MCMB), hereafter "the Board."

1.2 The Board operates the Marrickville Community Market precinct, comprising the Saturday growers' market, the Sunday craft and second-hand market, the community kitchen, and the storage and loading areas bounded by Illawarra Road and the railway corridor.

1.3 The purposes of the Board are:
(a) to provide a safe, accessible, and welcoming market environment for stallholders, shoppers, and the wider Marrickville community;
(b) to manage the market precinct in a financially responsible and environmentally sustainable manner;
(c) to support local producers, makers, and small businesses;
(d) to resolve disputes and address safety concerns in a fair, timely, and transparent manner; and
(e) to maintain the market as a community asset in accordance with the values of the Inner West Council.

---

PART 2 – MEMBERSHIP

2.1 The Board shall consist of no fewer than five (5) and no more than nine (9) voting members.

2.2 Membership categories:
(a) Elected members – up to five (5), elected at the Annual General Meeting;
(b) Council-appointed members – up to two (2), appointed by the Inner West Council;
(c) Community representatives – up to two (2), co-opted by the Board for their skills or community links.

2.3 The following persons are ineligible for membership:
(a) persons who are undischarged bankrupts;
(b) persons who have been convicted of an offence involving dishonesty within the preceding five (5) years;
(c) persons who are employees of the Board, other than the Market Manager who may attend meetings in an advisory capacity; and
(d) persons who hold a stallholder licence with the Market and are in arrears of fees or under active suspension.

2.5 A member may resign by written notice to the Secretary. The Board may remove a member by resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of the remaining members, on grounds of:
(a) three (3) consecutive unexcused absences from Board meetings;
(b) serious breach of this charter or the Code of Conduct; or
(c) conduct that brings the Board into disrepute.

2.6 The Board shall maintain a current Membership Register, to be reviewed at the first meeting of each financial year.

---

PART 3 – OFFICE HOLDERS

The charter specifies that the Trust and Safety Committee has a meeting_quorum of 3 members. Record status: current.

3.1 At the first meeting following each AGM, the Board shall elect from among its members:
(a) a Chair;
(b) a Deputy Chair;
(c) a Secretary; and
(d) a Treasurer.

3.2 The Chair presides at all meetings of the Board. In the Chair's absence, the Deputy Chair presides. If both are absent, the members present shall elect a chair for that meeting from among themselves.

3.3 The Secretary is responsible for:
(a) issuing notices of meetings;
(b) keeping minutes and the attendance register;
(c) maintaining the Membership Register and the Subcommittee Register; and
(d) lodging required documents with the NSW Registrar of Community Organisations.

3.5 Office holders serve for one (1) year and may be re-elected.

---

---

PART 5 – SUBCOMMITTEES

5.1 The Board may establish subcommittees to carry out specific functions. Subcommittees report to the Board and act within the terms of reference set by the Board.

5.2 Subcommittees shall be established by resolution of the Board, which shall specify:
(a) the subcommittee's name and purpose;
(b) the number of members and how they are appointed;
(c) the quorum for meetings of the subcommittee;
(d) the powers delegated to the subcommittee; and
(e) the reporting arrangements and review date.

(c) ensuring minutes are kept and lodged with the Secretary within seven (7) days of each meeting; and
(d) presenting the subcommittee’s report to the Board at the next ordinary Board meeting.

5.4 A subcommittee may co-opt additional persons with relevant expertise, provided that:
(a) co-opted members do not count toward the subcommittee’s quorum;
(b) co-opted members have no voting rights; and
(c) the number of co-opted members does not exceed the number of appointed members.

5.5 Unless otherwise specified in the terms of reference, subcommittees shall meet at least once every two (2) months. Additional meetings may be called by the Convenor or at the request of the Board.

5.6 The Board may dissolve or reconstitute a subcommittee at any time by resolution. Upon dissolution, the subcommittee shall deliver all records and any unspent funds to the Secretary within fourteen (14) days.

5.7 Standing subcommittees as at the date of adoption of this charter:

(a) Finance and Audit Subcommittee – oversees the Market’s budget, financial reporting, and the annual independent review; quorum of three (3) members;
(b) Trust and Safety Subcommittee – oversees stallholder compliance, incident review, and the development of safety procedures; quorum of three (3) members;
(c) Events and Promotion Subcommittee – advises on market programming, marketing, and community engagement; quorum of three (3) members; and
(d) Membership and Conduct Subcommittee – reviews applications for stallholder licences, handles complaints, and makes recommendations on disciplinary matters; quorum of three (3) members.

5.8 Each standing subcommittee shall review its terms of reference at least once every two (2) years and report any proposed changes to the Board for approval.

---

PART 6 – MEETINGS OF THE BOARD

6.1 Ordinary meetings of the Board shall be held at least once every two (2) months, at a time and place determined by the Board. The schedule of meetings for each financial year shall be adopted at the first Board meeting of that year.

6.2 The Secretary shall give at least seven (7) days’ written notice of each ordinary meeting, including the agenda. Notice may be given by electronic means to the address last notified by each member.

6.3 Special meetings may be called by the Chair, or by any three (3) members of the Board, by written request to the Secretary. The Secretary shall give at least forty-eight (48) hours’ notice of a special meeting, together with the business to be considered. No other business may be transacted at a special meeting.

6.4 A meeting of the Board is quorate if at least half of the current members, or five (5) members, whichever is the lesser, are present. For the avoidance of doubt, the quorum for the Trust and Safety Subcommittee remains as set out in its terms of reference.

6.5 Questions arising at a meeting shall be decided by a majority of votes of members present and voting. Each member has one (1) vote. In the case of an equality of votes, the Chair has a second or casting vote.

6.6 A member who has a material personal interest in a matter before the Board shall:
(a) disclose the nature of the interest before the matter is discussed;
(b) not be present while the matter is being considered, unless invited by the remaining members to assist; and
(c) not vote on the matter.

6.7 The Board may pass a resolution without a meeting if the resolution is signed or otherwise agreed in writing by all members entitled to vote on it. Such a resolution is taken to have been passed at a meeting of the Board held on the day the last member signs or agrees.

6.8 Minutes shall be kept of each meeting, including the names of members present, the matters considered, and the decisions made. Draft minutes shall be circulated within fourteen (14) days of the meeting and confirmed at the next ordinary meeting.
